div.l: I sey nat this yere so mery a cumpanye
At ones in this herber as ys now
Feyn wold I do yow myrthe and I wist how
And of a myrthe I am right now bethoght
To done yow ease and yt shall cost noght
Ye gone to Caunterbury god yow spede
That blisfull martir quite yoᵘ your mede
And wele I wote as ye gone by the wey
Ye shapen yow to talken and to pley
For trewly comforte ne mirthe is none
To ride by the wey as dom as it were a stone
And therfore will I make yow disport
As I seid erst and do yoᵘ som comfort
And yf yow like all by one assent
To stonde at my Iuggement
And for to werken as I shall yoᵘ sey
To morow whan ye ride by the wey
Now by my faders soule þat is dede
But ye be mery I will yeve yoᵘ my hede
Hold vp your hondes wᵗith out more speche
Our counseill was nat lang for to seche
Vs thought it was nat worthy to make yt wyse
And graunted hym wᵗithouten more avyse
And bade hym sey his veredit as him̄ lest
Lordyngᵉs qduod he now herkeneth for þe best
But take it nought I pray yow in disdeyn
This is the point to speke it short and pleyn
That ecch of yoᵘ to short with your wey
In this viage shall telle tales twey
To Caunterburyward I mene yt so
And homward he shall telle other two
Of auentures that whilom haue befalle
And which of yow that bereth hīm best of alle
That is to seyn that telleth in þis cas
Tales of most sentence and solas
Shall haue a soper at our alder cost
Here in this place sittyng by this post
Whan þat we com agein from Caunterbury
And for to make yow þe more mury
I will my self godely wᵗith yow ride
